title: Say it plainly: some things are not up for trade.
subtitle: The answer to a compromise offer
then: The Quraysh chiefs, Maududi says, still hoped for a compromise. Ibn Kathir reports {trap}they invited the Prophet ﷺ to worship their idols for a year, and they would worship his God for a year{/trap}. Allah answered with this surah, which the Prophet ﷺ often recited {reward}in the two rakahs before Fajr{/reward}.
now: Your manager suggests cutting a corner just this once. Friends push you to skip prayer for the trip. Not a fight, just a nice offer to meet in the middle. {idea}This surah teaches you how to say no calmly{/idea}, without anger and without wobbling.
old: Keeping the peace means meeting everyone halfway on everything.
new: I can be kind and still hold a line on what I worship and obey.
try: Recite this surah in your next sunnah prayer before Fajr or after Maghrib.

title: I do not worship what you worship. Not now.
subtitle: A clear statement about the present
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {trap}statues and rival gods{/trap}. Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ {idea}to disavow their religion completely{/idea}. The first line is about right now: I do not.
now: You may never bow to a statue. But the phone you check before you pray, the boss whose approval decides your mood, the follower count you refresh. {idea}What gets your first attention is close to what you serve.{/idea} Say this verse to those too.
old: I would never worship anything except Allah.
new: Worship includes what I obey and put first. I say no to every rival, not just statues.
try: Notice the first thing you reach for when you wake tomorrow. Let it be Allah's name.

title: And you are not worshipping the One I worship.
subtitle: Two objects of worship, not the same
then: Ibn Kathir says the One worshipped is {idea}Allah alone, Who has no partner{/idea}. He notes that the word ma (what) here means man (who). The Quraysh worshipped Allah {trap}alongside partners{/trap}, and that is not the same worship.
now: You pray to Allah, and then quietly add others: a lucky charm in the car, a feeling that your success depends on a person. {idea}Worship mixed with partners is not the worship Allah asks for.{/idea} Look for anything you have quietly added.
old: As long as I believe in Allah, a few extra habits do not matter.
new: Allah is worshipped alone. Anything I add beside Him changes the worship.
try: Remove one object or habit you rely on for luck or protection besides Allah.

title: Nor will I ever worship the way you worship.
subtitle: Not only whom, but how

row.title: as Allah loves
sub: the way He is pleased with

then: Ibn Kathir explains this repetition differently: {idea}I do not worship according to your worship{/idea}, I do not go along with it. {reward}I only worship Allah in the manner He loves and is pleased with.{/reward}
now: There is a trend for everything, even spirituality: a custom ritual from a video, a habit invented by a group chat. {idea}This verse is about method.{/idea} You do not get to invent the way to Allah. He has already shown it through His Messenger ﷺ.
old: How I worship is up to me, as long as my intention is good.
new: Allah chose the way He is worshipped. Following it is part of sincerity.
try: Learn one sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ in prayer that you did not know before, and do it today.

title: Nor will you worship what I worship, by desire.
subtitle: Worship invented from the self

row.title: what I want it to be

then: Ibn Kathir says this second time means {trap}you do not follow Allah's commands; you have invented something out of the promptings of your own souls{/trap}. He cites: {idea}they follow a guess and what they desire, while guidance has come from their Lord{/idea}.
now: It is easy to keep the parts of religion that suit you and quietly drop the rest. The modest dress, the honest tax return, the patience with your parents. {trap}Picking by preference is the trap this verse names{/trap}. Turn it on yourself first.
old: I follow the parts of the religion that make sense to me.
new: When my desires edit my religion, I start worshipping my wants. I follow what Allah sent.
try: Pick one teaching you have been avoiding because it is inconvenient. Take one small step toward it.

title: Your way is yours, and mine is mine.
subtitle: A clear boundary, without a fight
then: Ibn Kathir links this to: {idea}for me are my deeds and for you are your deeds; you are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do{/idea}. The surah ends not with a threat but with {reward}a calm, clear line{/reward}.
now: You do not need to win every argument with the friend who mocks your faith, or prove yourself at every family gathering. {reward}You can simply live your deen, clearly and calmly.{/reward} Your job is your own deeds.
old: Standing firm in my faith means arguing with everyone who disagrees.
new: I can hold my deen clearly and calmly. My deeds are mine to answer for.
try: The next time someone challenges your faith, answer with one calm sentence and then let it go.
